hints: Look at the relative enthalpy levels in the diagram and decide whether heat is absorbed or released.
Recall that breaking a lattice, breaking a covalent bond, and removing water from a hydrated ion all require energy input.
Check each of the three given processes to see if bonds or attractions are broken with no new stronger bonds formed, making all of them endothermic.
walkthrough:
**Read the energy profile**

Products are drawn higher than reactants, so enthalpy increases during the reaction. That means heat is taken in.

$$\Delta H = H(\text{products}) - H(\text{reactants}) > 0$$

**Link shape to reaction type**

A positive $\Delta H$ means an endothermic reaction. We need processes where energy must be supplied to break strong attractions or bonds.

**Test reaction 1**

$\text{CaCO}_3(\text{s}) \rightarrow \text{CaO}(\text{s}) + \text{CO}_2(\text{g})$ is thermal decomposition. Breaking the ionic lattice and covalent bonds needs continuous heating, so it is endothermic.

**Test reaction 2 and reaction 3**

$\text{H}_2(\text{g}) \rightarrow 2\text{H}(\text{g})$ breaks an $\text{H-H}$ covalent bond, bond breaking is always endothermic. $\text{Cl}^-(\text{aq}) \rightarrow \text{Cl}^-(\text{g}) + \text{aq}$ is the reverse of hydration, ion-dipole attractions are broken, so it is also endothermic.

All three fit the diagram, giving 1, 2 and 3.

options.A: Correct. All three reactions are endothermic with products at higher enthalpy than reactants. Thermal decomposition, bond dissociation and dehydration of an ion all require energy input.
options.B: Incorrect. This combination leaves out reaction 3. Students sometimes think $\text{Cl}^-(\text{aq}) \rightarrow \text{Cl}^-(\text{g})$ is exothermic, but hydration $\text{Cl}^-(\text{g}) \rightarrow \text{Cl}^-(\text{aq})$ is exothermic, so the reverse process is endothermic.
options.C: Incorrect. This combination leaves out reaction 1. Students sometimes confuse decomposition of a carbonate with combustion, but $\text{CaCO}_3$ decomposition needs strong heating and is clearly endothermic.
options.D: Incorrect. This selects only one reaction. Each process involves only breaking of bonds or attractions (lattice, H-H bond, ion-water attractions) with no compensating bond formation, so all three are endothermic.
